speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand this newborn is having trouble feeding and vomiting green fluid; when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant have any visible abdominal distension or tenderness upon palpation? I also need to know if the baby has passed meconium yet, and if so, how long after birth it occurred.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the infant has not passed meconium yet, which is concerning given the bilious vomiting and abdominal distension. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-Ray reveals a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "double bubble" sign on your X-ray is highly suggestive of duodenal atresia, a blockage in the small intestine. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.
